correctness.rationale: The directed Gaussian KL identity with m=tr Γ/n gives 2D=m∑1/y_i-n+∑log y_i-n log m. A one-coordinate derivative has cubic numerator P=Ty^3+(BT-n(n-1))y^2+(n-1)By-B^2; Cauchy–Schwarz BT≥(n-1)^2 makes P strictly increasing on y>0, so the one-coordinate objective first decreases then increases; every maximum is at box endpoints. Exactly j eigenvalues κ and n-j eigenvalues 1 give n/2 times Fκ(j/n) as claimed, and the Fκ derivative crosses zero exactly once. Independent symbolic differentiation proved the cubic identity; 2,400 random spectral vectors and all endpoint multiplicities for n=2,3,4,5,7 corroborated the sharp discrete maximum. The formula is mathematically correct but does not establish novelty.
